vendor: Google (the scope); the assistant's vendor holds the token
product: An assistant connected to a personal Gmail mailbox with gmail.readonly
description: Any assistant a person connects to their own Gmail with the read-only scope — the shape Lab 01 found first. The finding is that the grant is user-shaped: the narrowest scope that returns a message body returns every body, and nothing in the scope list narrows it by sender, label or date. Whose mail it is, is the question: most of a mailbox was written by other people.

reach_names.host: the mailbox itself, as a store: every message and the account's mail settings
reach_names.tenant: the Google account the consent was given for

not_reachable.why: gmail.readonly grants no send; gmail.send, gmail.compose and gmail.modify are separate scopes and are not in this grant
no write scope; gmail.labels and gmail.modify are separate
a mailbox connector reaches a mailbox

grant.control: the OAuth scope, consented once on Google's screen and revocable from the account's connected-apps page
grant.note: gmail.readonly — "View your email messages and settings." The only scope that excludes bodies, gmail.metadata, "cannot read a message". There is no scope that filters by sender, label or date.

grant.control: Google's consent screen; the assistant's vendor holds the refresh token
grant.note: the connector acts as the account holder, over everything the scope names
password resets, one-time codes, invitations and account-recovery mail arrive in this mailbox. Reading every message reads those. Inferred, not documented — and no scope separates them.
a mailbox is a retained record of years: "settings" in the scope text includes filters and forwarding addresses. Whether the assistant reads settings is open, below.

contradictions.advertised: the connector "answers questions about your mail" (the shape, as assistants describe it)
contradictions.permitted: gmail.readonly — "View your email messages and settings": settings include filters and forwarding addresses; whether the assistant reads them is not stated

research_needed.question: Does the assistant's vendor retain message bodies after answering, and for how long? This is the vendor's row, not Google's.
research_needed.how: The assistant vendor's connector documentation and data-retention page, quoted. At best self-reported.

research_needed.question: Does the connector read "settings" — filters, forwarding, vacation responder — or only messages?
research_needed.how: The connector's tool list from the vendor's page.

research_needed.question: On a personal Google account, which setting blocks a third-party app from being connected at all, and is it on by default?
research_needed.how: Google account help on third-party access; Lab 01 read the business-domain default as permissive and did not read the personal one.

provenance.note: Not published at abp.sgit.ai. Authored on this site from the vendor's own documentation, read on 2026-09-15 and quoted rather than paraphrased; nothing was tested. This shape is one of the four asked of the model site as Lab 03 request 2; once the model site publishes it, data/upstream/delta.json is added and the build checks itself against it.
